text.p: The Malaysian Airline System Bhd (MAS) is reorganising its top management as part of efforts to rejuvenate the once state-run national airline, the daily Star newspaper said on Saturday.
The newspaper said MAS was creating three new positions for executive vice presidents with effect from this month, taking their total number to 11.
MAS officials were not available for comment on Saturday, but the newspaper said a spokeswoman for the airline confirmed the changes.

The Star said MAS chairman Tajudin Ramli issued a circular to the company's staff last week outlining areas to focus on for greater competency. They are passenger services, ground services, engineering, catering and cargo handling.

"In order to intensify our efforts to achieve the parallel goal of transforming the company into a more successful and most respected airline in the world, further realignment needs to be introduced to the management process of the company," Tajudin was quoted as saying in the circular.
Tajudin took control of the privatised airline in 1994.
